For the Petitioner : Mr. Sushant Kumar Sinha, Advocate For the State : Mr. Naveen Kr. Gaunjhu,
A.P.P. .....
Order No.03/ Dated:21.02.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Hunterganj P.S. Case No. 04 of 2018 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 56 of 2018 instituted under Sections 353, 420, 183, 279, 336, 201, 120(B), 224 and 225 of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per F.I.R. allegation is that petitioner is the owner of the seized vehicle which was involved in carrying sand illegally from the river, along with other accused persons.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is submitted that other similarly situated co- accused person, namely, Gaurishankar Kushwaha has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in A.B.A. No. 11497 of 2022 vide order dated 01.02.2023.

It is lastly submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation coupled with materials on record, I am inclined to grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court below within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Chatra in connection with Hunterganj P.S. Case No. 04 of 2018 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 56 of 2018 with the condition that he will co-operate with the Ramratan Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand ......Opposite ... on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81609493/
1 investigation of the case and appear before the investigating officer as and when noticed by him and furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
